name: Verdant Athletic
history: Founded by glasshouse gardeners on the edge of Larkhaven, Verdant built their name on patient, possession-first football. Three league titles in the 1960s gave way to forty lean years before a youth-led revival returned them to the top four. Supporters still bring sprigs of fern to the first home match of each season.
crest_brief: A fern frond curling inside a hexagonal glasshouse pane, gold outline on deep green, founding year beneath.

name: Ironvale Forge
history: The works team of the Ironvale foundries, Forge play with the directness of the town that made them. Their rivalry with Verdant dates from two bitter cup finals in 1974 and 1975, each settled in extra time. A high-pressing reinvention under their current coach has made them the league's most feared away side.
crest_brief: Crossed tongs over an anvil, red on black, with three sparks above.

name: Saltmarsh Mariners
history: A harbour club whose ground sits close enough to the water that clearances are fished out by the harbour master. The Mariners prize wide play and crossing, and have produced more full-backs for the national side than any other club in the league.
crest_brief: A stylised lighthouse with a single beam crossing a wave, blue and white, rope border.

name: Northmoor Wanderers
history: The league's oldest club, founded by moorland walkers who played wherever the heather was short. Northmoor favour a compact mid-block and quick counters, and their home crowd is famous for a minute's silence broken by a single bugle call before every derby.
crest_brief: A bugle over a sprig of heather, purple and silver, inside a shield with a walking-stick border.

name: Copperdene Rangers
history: Born in the pottery district and named for the copper glaze that made the town rich, Rangers have spent most of their history between the top two divisions. They are the league's best side at set pieces and its most patient in a low block.
crest_brief: A kiln chimney with a copper flame, orange on charcoal, circular badge.

name: Westhollow Harriers
history: Formed by a running club that wanted a winter sport, the Harriers still run their pre-season on the same hill trail. They play the fastest tempo in the league and concede the most counter-attacks because of it.
crest_brief: A harrier hawk in flight over a lantern, teal and white, minimal line art.

name: Granite Hill
history: A quarrying town's club with a reputation for the tallest back line in the league. Granite Hill were promoted last season for the first time in a generation and survive on aerial strength and a goalkeeper who has saved more penalties than anyone in the division.
crest_brief: A cut granite block with a yellow chisel mark, grey and yellow, square badge.

name: Brackenford Town
history: The youngest club in the league, founded by mill workers after the town's old club folded. Brackenford play an expansive 4-3-3 with inverted full-backs and lean on the league's most productive academy.
crest_brief: A mill wheel with fronds of bracken, magenta and white, round badge.
